title: Per-endpoint SLI calibration and error-budget arbitration playbook for tiered tenant prioritization
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Purpose: Define a reproducible, per-endpoint SLI calibration process and an operational error-budget arbitration policy that supports multi-tenant, multi-region deployments. This ticket produces a playbook that engineers and SREs can follow to: (1) declare SLIs tied to observable signals; (2) calibrate thresholds by traffic class and model characteristics; (3) assign error-budget currency and priority bands for tenants; (4) automate arbitration decisions during cross-region capacity constraints; and (5) provide a clear runbook for applying circuit breakers and progressive load-shedding while preserving highest-priority SLAs.
acceptance_criteria: A single canonical SLI declaration template (CSV + example) exists for per-endpoint latency, availability, and response-quality signals and is stored at the SLO Confluence page.

Calibration scripts that ingest recent 90-day telemetry and output candidate thresholds (P50/P95/P99 latency, success-rate) per model family are committed to infra/slo-calibration and pass CI with synthetic data.

An error-budget arbitration algorithm (spec + pseudocode) is published that supports: reserved budget bands, tenant borrowing, and regional escrow; the algorithm is covered by unit tests and a simulation harness.
Grafana dashboard with arbitration signals (budget burn rate, regional spare capacity, active circuit-breakers, tenant priorities) is live in prod-preview and linked from the playbook.

Runbook: clear steps for SRE on when to trigger controlled preemptive shedding, how to apply soft vs hard circuit-breakers, and the rollback criteria for tenant-impacting actions are documented and reviewed by oncall SREs.
Documented ratified decision on how response-quality regressions (detected by eval prompts) count against error budgets vs being treated as separate quality incidents.
implementation_steps: Draft SLI declaration template: fields, units, aggregation windows, TTLs for derived metrics (owner: Marco)
Build calibration pipeline: ETL of telemetry -> per-model distribution analysis -> candidate SLO thresholds (owner: Reliability team)
Design arbitration model: fixed bands (Gold/Silver/Bronze), borrowing rules, escrow release conditions, and hysteresis for circuit-breakers (owner: SRE)
Implement simulation harness: replay historical traffic with failover scenarios and verify arbitration outcomes match policy expectations
Create Grafana dashboards and alert rules for: burn-rate > X, cross-region capacity < Y, active arbitration events
PR: SDK to expose arbitration decisions to Console and API layer so Console can surface live tenant priority decisions
Review and tabletop: runbook drill with SRE, PM, and SOC to validate decision clarity
Ship: merge calibration scripts and arbitration library; update Confluence playbook; announce in #reliability and weekly reliability sync
decisions: SLI surface will include: latency (P95, P99, tail-quantile), success-rate (HTTP 2xx + model semantic success), and response-quality (eval-prompt pass rate).
Error-budget currency: hours-equivalent burn (normalized by route token-weighted cost) to allow fair cross-model comparison.
Tenant priority bands will be Gold/Silver/Bronze with Gold allocated a guaranteed escrow slice per region; Gold can borrow from global escrow under defined conditions.
Circuit-breaker modes: soft (response-truncation + degrade model variant) vs hard (reject + 429) with configurable hysteresis windows to avoid flapping.

Quality regressions detected by automated evals are rate-limited against budgets: small regressions increment a quality-led burn counter; large regressions trigger immediate safeguards and a manual incident review.
tradeoffs: Strict per-endpoint SLOs increase operational overhead and alert noise for low-volume routes; mitigated by grouping low-traffic routes into 'micro' SLO buckets.
Normalizing error budgets by token-cost enables fair comparisons across models but introduces billing coupling; decided to expose both raw-token burn and normalized currency.
Aggressive soft-shedding preserves availability but risks subtle quality degradation for lower-priority tenants; mitigation: apply quality-based throttles and canary experiments before broad rollout.
